production_findings.finding: release_usage_receipt(&_usage) removes the returned query-vector capacity charge while the named _usage binding still owns its allocation. ValueContext::capture and retain_static_host_invocation may allocate afterward, before that binding is dropped at scope exit. Requests combining actual queries with retained values/host calls can therefore have a real receipt/backing overlap absent from the live-byte ledger.
production_findings.required_correction: Discard the receipt allocation before subsequent allocating consumers and before releasing its capacity charge, e.g. save capacity, drop the receipt, then release; alternatively use a consuming release API. A passing VM-only peak test does not cover this driver successor lifetime.

production_findings.status: Open at exact f47e1bb5; reported to root; inherited release site
production_findings.finding: program_copy_cost(&expected) is reserved before expected.clone() becomes raw and then the owned verified artifact. copied_bytes is released before verified.program() supplies result_type and before ValueContext::capture consumes the verified program. The verified allocation remains owned across those later allocations, so releasing its charge there understates the actual overlap.
production_findings.required_correction: Retain the copy charge through all verified-program consumers; drop verified before releasing the charge and before later host-retention allocations, or explicitly retain the charge for the true remaining lifetime. This is distinct from the VM pending/frame release already repaired.

concrete_boundaries_confirmed: Actual Unit Call is the sole no-result exception in CT Verify, after checking real target existence, source authority/visibility, arity and each argument type. Non-Unit Call and unrelated Unit instructions retain result-presence obligations. Function Return(None) still requires the declared actual Unit result.

The observing VM saves caller/block/instruction/callee/result before entering a callee and publishes that event only after normal Return. Unit calls use exact instruction ordinals, not a missing-result fallback. Repeated calls remain separate events; failed whole evaluation returns no event vector. The ordinary evaluator passes no collector and pays no collection work.

Pending and completed event vectors prepay full new backing and old-element copy work before growth, release old backing after replacement, and successful outer cleanup retains the actual returned completed capacity. At root Return the VM now drops pending_calls and frames before releasing those backing charges, then allocates the query receipt. This closes the specific earlier VM overlap; the separate driver findings above remain.

The 4a529 controls use a verified raw CFG containing eight actual Unit calls plus a real query receipt. They assert all eight complete locations, Unit output, unchanged ordinary VM steps, observer-only analysis work, exact temporary N/N-1/fresh and failed-request cleanup. Six raw/Wire malformed neighbors cover non-Unit missing result, missing target, unauthorized symbol, arity, operand type and unrelated Unit instruction. These are VM/raw evidence, not Source evidence.
